sentences.en: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 你好,这是6分钟英语 从英国广播公司学习英语。

sentences.en: I'm Beth. And I'm Pippa. Everywhere you look online, from gaming and fashion to music, travel and culture, you'll find social media influencers.
sentences.zh: 我是贝丝,我叫皮帕,不管你在网上看什么, 从游戏和时尚到音乐,旅行和文化,你都会发现社交媒体的影响者。

sentences.en: These social media influencers do what they're famous for: influencing and creating trends.
sentences.zh: 这些社交媒体影响者 做他们著名的: 影响和创造趋势。

sentences.en: Do you follow any social media influencers, Beth?
sentences.zh: 你跟踪任何社交媒体影响者吗,贝丝?

sentences.en: Erm… I don't follow any specifically, I would say, but I do see influencers on Facebook and Instagram – things like that.
sentences.zh: 但我确实在Facebook和Instagram上看到过影响力人物,

sentences.en: Well, the most successful influencers have millions of followers and, not surprisingly, this has caught the attention of another group of people trying to get their message out to the public: politicians.
sentences.zh: 最成功的影响力者 拥有数百万的追随者 毫不奇怪 这引起了另一群人的关注

sentences.en: Politicians using the media to win elections is nothing new but, in this episode, we'll be finding out what happens when social media influencers become politicians themselves.
sentences.zh: 政治人物利用媒体赢得选举并非新鲜事,

sentences.en: As usual, we'll be learning some useful new words and phrases, and remember – there's a transcript of this episode to read along with while you listen.
sentences.zh: 和往常一样,我们会学习一些有用的新词句, 并记住—— 当你聆听时,这集的笔录会和你们一起阅读。

sentences.en: It's available now on our website: bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 现可在我们的网站上查阅:bbc学习英语.com。

sentences.en: But first, I have a question for you, Beth.
sentences.zh: 但首先,我有一个问题问你,贝丝。

sentences.en: The most followed Instagram account of 2025 belongs to footballer Cristiano Ronaldo, but how many followers does he have? a) 6.7 million, b) 67 million, or c) 667 million?
sentences.zh: 2025年的Instagram账户中, 最多的是足球运动员Cristiano Ronaldo, 但他有多少追随者? a) 670万,b) 6 700万,或c) 6.67亿?

sentences.en: Ooh… I'm going to go down the middle: 67 million.
sentences.zh: 我要从中间下去 6700万

sentences.en: Well, we'll find out the answer later in the programme.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后在节目里会找到答案的

sentences.en: Around the world, politicians are realising that they can reach a lot of people through social media influencers.
sentences.zh: 世界各地政治人物都认识到,

sentences.en: There have even been allegations of politicians paying for the support of influencers in places like Colombia, Argentina and Indonesia.
sentences.zh: 甚至有人指控,在哥伦比亚、阿根廷和印度尼西亚等地,政客付钱支持影响力人物。

sentences.en: And one place where politics has become a big topic on social media is Nigeria.
sentences.zh: 政治成为社会媒体重要话题的地方是尼日利亚。

sentences.en: Nigeria is a country with a huge, young population.
sentences.zh: 尼日利亚是一个人口众多、年轻的国家。

sentences.en: There are around 200 million people in total and 70% of them are under 30.
sentences.zh: 总人数约为2亿人,其中70%在30岁以下。

sentences.en: Many of these young voters are turned off, meaning not interested, in traditional media, but they do follow social media influencers.
sentences.zh: 许多年轻选民对传统媒体不感兴趣,

sentences.en: Adline Okere is BBC Igbo news editor in Lagos, Nigeria.
sentences.zh: Adline Okere是尼日利亚拉各斯BBC Igbo新闻编辑。

sentences.en: She spoke with BBC World Service programme The Fifth Floor about the situation there: Influencers are super important to shaping the narrative of these young people.
sentences.zh: 她与英国广播公司世界服务局的第五层节目讨论了那里的情况:影响因素对于塑造这些年轻人的叙事极为重要。

sentences.en: Some of them started in, you know, activism.
sentences.zh: 其中一些开始,你知道的, 活动。

sentences.en: Some of them started out with lifestyle and then branched into politics.
sentences.zh: 他们中有些人从生活方式开始,然后从政治中分裂出来。

sentences.en: Adline thinks influencers are super important in Nigerian politics.
sentences.zh: Adline认为影响者在尼日利亚政治中非常重要。

sentences.en: She uses super to mean very, extremely, or more than usual.
sentences.zh: 她用超人的意思是非常, 极端,或超过通常。

sentences.en: For example, if you say you're super happy about something, you mean you're very happy about it.
sentences.zh: 比如说,如果你说你对某事超级高兴, 你是说你对它非常高兴。

sentences.en: In Nigeria, influencers are shaping the narrative of elections.
sentences.zh: 在尼日利亚,影响者正在塑造选举的叙事。

sentences.en: If someone shapes a narrative, they have a strong influence over how something is presented or understood.
sentences.zh: 如果有人塑造一个叙事,他们就会对某种东西的表达或理解产生强大的影响。

sentences.en: Influencing things, of course, is exactly what influencers do, but now, more and more social media personalities are branching out into politics.
sentences.zh: 影响事物,当然, 恰恰是影响者做的, 但现在,越来越多的社交媒体人物 正在走向政治。

sentences.en: When you branch out, you start doing something different from what you usually do, such as a new activity or job.
sentences.zh: 当你分头工作时,你开始做与通常不同的事情,比如新的活动或工作。

sentences.en: So, what happens when influencers become politicians themselves?
sentences.zh: 那么,当影响者自己成为政治家时会发生什么呢?

sentences.en: Here, Adline Okere explains more to Faranak Amidi, presenter of BBC World Service's The Fifth Floor: What about in Nigeria?
sentences.zh: Adline Okere向BBC世界服务局的主持人Faranak Amidi解释更多:在尼日利亚呢?

sentences.en: Is there a pushback against these influencers who got involved in promoting political parties?
sentences.zh: 是否有人反对那些参与推动政党的影响力人物?

sentences.en: Absolutely – a huge pushback! They will also go back and dig up information about these people from their personal lives and then publish them on social media.
sentences.zh: 绝对 — — 巨大的回击。 他们还会回去从个人生活中挖掘关于这些人的信息,然后在社交媒体上公布。

sentences.en: In Nigeria, there was a pushback against social media influencers turned politicians.
sentences.zh: 在尼日利亚, 社会媒体影响者转而成为政治人物,

sentences.en: A pushback is a negative reaction or rejection of something that has happened.
sentences.zh: 退缩就是消极反应或拒绝已经发生的事情。

sentences.en: In fact, the public reaction was so bad, people started to dig up information about influencers who promote politicians.
sentences.zh: 事实上,公众的反应如此糟糕, 人们开始挖掘信息 有关影响者 谁促进政客。

sentences.en: If you dig up information about someone, you try to find details about them.
sentences.zh: 如果你发现了关于某人的信息, 你试着找到关于他们的细节。

sentences.en: We have a similar phrase – dig up dirt on someone, which means trying to find information about someone which could damage their reputation.
sentences.zh: 我们也有类似的说法 — — 在某人身上挖土,这意味着试图找到可能损害其声誉的人的信息。

sentences.en: So, social media can be a powerful tool for politicians but getting involved in politics doesn't always go well for social media influencers.
sentences.zh: 因此,社交媒体可以成为政治家的有力工具, 但参与政治对社交媒体的影响力者来说并不总是很好。

sentences.en: OK. Pippa, isn't it time you revealed the answer to your question?
sentences.zh: 皮帕,你是不是该透露答案了?

sentences.en: Yes, I asked, "How many followers does Cristiano Ronaldo, the footballer, have?" And the answer was c) 667 million, at the time of recording.
sentences.zh: 是的,我问,“足球运动员克里斯蒂亚诺·罗纳尔多有多少追随者?” 答案是(c)6.67亿,在记录时。

sentences.en: That's a lot more than I have, Beth. And me... wow!
sentences.zh: 这比我还多 贝丝 还有我...

sentences.en: OK. Let's recap the vocabulary we've learned, starting with the phrasal verb turned off, meaning uninterested.
sentences.zh: 好吧,让我们回顾一下我们学到的词汇, 从句子动词关闭开始, 意思是不感兴趣的。

sentences.en: When super is placed before an adjective, it means very or more than usual.
sentences.zh: 当超级被置于一个形容词之前时,它的意义就比通常的要大。

sentences.en: Social media influencers who shape the narrative have a strong influence over how something is presented or understood.
sentences.zh: 社会媒体的影响力影响着故事的表达或理解。

sentences.en: If you branch out into something new, you start doing an activity or job that is different from what you usually do.
sentences.zh: 如果分化成新的东西, 你开始做一个 与通常不同的活动或工作。

sentences.en: A pushback is a negative reaction to something new that has happened.
sentences.zh: 退缩就是对新事物的消极反应

sentences.en: And finally, the phrasal verb dig up means to try and find information.
sentences.zh: 最后, 语句动词挖掘 意味着尝试寻找信息。

sentences.en: This is often about a person and their private life in order to try and damage their reputation.
sentences.zh: 这往往关系到一个人和他们的私生活,以便试图损害他们的声誉。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up, but why not head over to our website, bbclearningenglish.com, to try the quiz and worksheet for this episode?
sentences.zh: 我们的六分钟又到了 但是为什么不直接去我们的网站,bbclearingenglish.com, 来试试这个片段的测验和工作表呢?

sentences.en: See you there soon, but for now, goodbye!
sentences.zh: 一会儿见,但现在再见!

sentences.en: Bye!
sentences.zh: 再见!
